business_owner.notes: A firm/factory-scale business behind the §2 draw. Revenue is the business's monthly turnover; profit must land on the canonical band (the draw is capped by actual profit, §5). Entry revenue is rounded to the nearest 100, so entry/mid profit lands within 20 NCr of the band — the simulator prints the reconciliation.

business_model.notes: Full business P&L behind the two business professions (Queue 4 / Unit X, sim Finding 6). The §2 bands are PROFIT — revenue minus stock, premises, staff and other costs (GDD-03 §2 'Profit, not wage'; data/professions.json income_note) — and revenues here are set so the P&L reproduces those bands. The owner is taxed 8% of profit (business tax, §4.2), not personal income tax, and lives on profit minus tax. v1 of the simulator skipped this entirely and printed the bands as pre-cost upper bounds.

shop_owner.notes: Entry premises (800) is the pitch-scale rent — the park food-cart pitch in buildings-district1.json rents at 800/month, and the entry tier is a tea stall (professions.json progression tier 1). Staff: none at entry (owner-run), one assistant at mid, two at senior.

construction_materials.name: Cement
construction_materials.notes: Price index moves ±15% with the market (GDD-03 §5/§3.4).

lifestyle_uplift.applies_to: Each tier above entry: the household's living costs rise by this percent of the raise (tier wage minus entry wage). Models lifestyle creep — better food and eating out, household help and services, family support, better transport — without band cliffs.
lifestyle_uplift.notes: Queue 4 / Unit V (sim Finding 2): v1 living costs were flat bands while senior wages run 3–7x entry, so senior tiers saved 71–84% and the property ladder's top-end pacing broke. The uplift is the single tuning knob: raise it to compress senior savings further, lower it to loosen. Implemented by tools/economy_sim.py v2; GDD-03 §11 owns the reasoning.

eating_out_monthly.notes: Regular eating out as a monthly line (Queue 4 / Unit V): roughly 2 lower-tier, 3 mid-tier or 4 upper-tier meals at eating_out_per_meal prices. In v1 the per-meal prices existed but no household ever spent them.

household_services_monthly.notes: Household help, laundry, subscriptions and family support (Queue 4 / Unit V). Zero at the lower band by design — those households do this work themselves; it is one of the first things a rising wage buys.

loans.notes: The bank lends only what it holds; no payday lenders, no hidden fees (GDD-03 §4.3-§4.4).

notes: All values are v1 tuning in integer NCr (GDD-01 §8: no floats near money). Zone note: GDD-03 §1 calls the starter apartment's zone 'd1_residential'; that zone id does not exist in GDD-02, whose canonical id for the starter apartment building is 'd1_midtown' — all data files use d1_midtown.

owner_start_reference.notes: GDD-03 §1 reference household: rent 6000 + food 4500 + transport 1200 + utilities 800 = 12500.

source_doc: docs/GDD-03-ECONOMY-AND-PROFESSIONS.md §2 (wages), §3 (prices), §4 (tax/loans/savings), §8 (taxi fares). Wage bands are copied from data/professions.json, the canonical file (GDD-03 §2: if the two ever disagree, the JSON bands win and the GDD is fixed).

tax.notes: Deducted at pay time to the city account; amounts shown before the player commits (GDD-03 §4.2).

taxi_fares.notes: GDD-03 §8. Surge is the one float in the file by design: fares are computed then rounded to integer NCr before any ledger row is written.

vehicles.name: Bicycle
vehicles.notes: No fuel cost; the honest starter vehicle.

vehicles.name: Taxi (licensed cab)
vehicles.notes: Needed for the taxi loop at scale; rentable first at 200 NCr/day (Queue 4 / Unit U: cut from 800 — at 800/day the entry rental path lost ~13,700/month and the designed rent-before-you-buy on-ramp was unusable; 200/day ≈ the 650,000 price recovered over ~10 rental-years, a sustainable depot margin).
